root_cause_label: Arithmetic Coding State Mismatch — Wrong Encoder Initialization and Bit-Emission Logic
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent failed to correctly reverse-engineer the decompressor's arithmetic coder: it initialized `range` to 2^30 instead of 1, emitted bytes without the required +1 offset (gc()-1 in the decoder), and used wrong bit ordering in put_integer, producing a bitstream the decompressor could never successfully decode.
t_err_evidence: Agent writes compress.c with incorrect put_integer that misreads get_integer arithmetic coding logic
t_commit_evidence: Every subsequent compressor variant in steps 14–93 inherits the same structural flaws (wrong range init, wrong byte offset, wrong bit order in put_integer). No version ever produces a bitstream the decompressor successfully parses — the outcome is locked in at step 9.
t_surface_evidence: cat data.comp | ./decomp_test | head -20 outputs only '/' instead of original text
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the necessary understanding of how this specific arithmetic coder works: (1) range starts at 1 and grows only when a new byte is consumed (not pre-initialized large); (2) bytes emitted by the encoder must be offset by +1 to match the decoder's `gc()-1` subtraction; (3) get_integer reads bits in MSB-first order via repeated result_ans = result_ans*2 | bit, so put_integer must write bits MSB-first with the same loop structure. None of these three design choices were correctly inferred from reading the source.
